facts.raw_span: skin-colored, dome-shaped firm papules over the chin, nose, and perinasal region
dozens of skin-colored dome-shaped papules over the chin, nasal, and perinasal regions of the face
No hypopigmented macules, periungual fibromas, or Shagreen plaques were present
several teeth with a conical shape
a dome-shaped lesion with several plump fibroblasts and increased blood vessels, compatible with an angiofibroma
No crystals were observed even with polarized light microscopy
a dermal fibroblast with prominent crystalline inclusions within the cytoplasm and some smaller inclusions forming within lysosomes
requiring a right renal transplant at age 14 years
the facial papules had increased in size and number since he first noticed them at about age 18 years

concepts.why: The presence of angiofibromas, renal disease history, and skin lesions supports this diagnosis.
The histologic analysis showing a dome-shaped lesion with plump fibroblasts and increased blood vessels is consistent with angiofibroma.
The history of renal transplant and possible underlying renal disease suggests a connection to nephrocalcinosis.

concepts.preferred_label: Dermal Fibroblast Disorder with Crystalline Inclusions
concepts.why: The electron microscopy findings of crystalline inclusions within dermal fibroblasts support this diagnosis.
The presence of conical-shaped teeth is a distinctive feature of certain genetic disorders.
The patient's history of renal transplant increases the risk of various complications.
The combination of skin-colored papules and dermal fibroblast abnormalities points towards a fibroblast disorder with skin manifestations.
The presence of multiple system involvement, including skin, teeth, and kidneys, suggests a genetic disorder with broad effects.

rationales.F01: The presence of skin-colored, dome-shaped firm papules is consistent with angiofibromas, which are a common feature of Tuberous Sclerosis Complex.
rationales.F02: The presence of dozens of skin-colored dome-shaped papules further supports the diagnosis of Tuberous Sclerosis Complex and angiofibroma.
rationales.F03: The absence of hypopigmented macules, periungual fibromas, and Shagreen plaques makes Tuberous Sclerosis Complex less likely, but does not rule it out.
rationales.F04: The presence of conical teeth is a feature of some genetic disorders, including Tuberous Sclerosis Complex.
rationales.F05: The histologic analysis showing a dome-shaped lesion with plump fibroblasts and increased blood vessels is consistent with an angiofibroma, which is a common feature of Tuberous Sclerosis Complex.
rationales.F07: The presence of crystalline inclusions within dermal fibroblasts is a distinctive feature of some fibroblast disorders, including Dermal Fibroblast Disorder with Crystalline Inclusions.
rationales.F08: The history of renal transplant at a young age may be related to a genetic disorder with multi-system involvement, such as Tuberous Sclerosis Complex.
